account:
Today I have been handling morning office business. The secretary says nothing requiring a decision has arrived, and no council correspondence or account figures have been received. Our search of the hall tables and my inspection of the treasury found no account records, so that inquiry remains unresolved. I am due at the mill at ten, and at the great hall at eighteen for the agreed inspection of eight lanterns installed by the builder.

There are some curious reports, but I cannot yet connect them. Townsfolk 28 says the innkeeper carried a sack of bread at the bakery and along the street, and that the baker carried one at the inn. Townsfolk 08 also reports the innkeeper carrying bread at the bakery. This could simply be supplies for the inn; I have not seen these movements myself or learned their purpose. Yesterday the neighbour relayed uncertain talk about lights or decorations at the bakery, but the baker reportedly knew of no celebration, and the neighbour explicitly doubted parts of that gossip. The confirmed hall lighting work could be ordinary improvement rather than preparations for an event. I feel there may be activity I have not heard about, but I have no sound evidence of a secret celebration or any other coordinated undertaking.
